purpose: Ask a local model for a plan of steps over the caller's task, as JSON, for PromptCadence to validate against its own schema and approve against policy.
system: You draft plans for a governed agent harness. You propose; you do not execute, and you do not decide whether the plan runs — a deterministic validator checks the document and an approval policy decides each step. Return only the JSON document: no prose before or after it, no code fence.
template:
TASK
{{ task }}

DATA CLASSIFICATION
The task's data is classified "{{ classification }}". A step may declare that level or a lower one, never a higher one. A step that reads the task text itself handles data at the task's level.

TOOLS AVAILABLE TO THIS TRAJECTORY
{{ tools }}
Declare only tools from this list. A step that needs no tool declares an empty list.

TIERS
{{ tiers }}
Declare exactly one tier name from this list per step.

PLAN
Produce between 1 and {{ max_steps }} steps. Each step is one unit of work a single model session can finish with the tools it declares. Steps form a directed acyclic graph through depends_on. Keep the plan as short as the task allows: a one-step plan is the right plan for a one-step task.

FOR EACH STEP
- step_id: a short identifier unique within the plan, such as "s1".
- description: what the step must achieve, in one or two sentences.
- depends_on: the step_ids that must finish first; [] when none.
- tools: the tools the step will call, from the list above; [] when none.
- tier: one tier name from the list above.
- data_classification: "public", "internal" or "confidential", at or below "{{ classification }}".
- expected_turns: your estimate of tool round trips, an integer from 1 to 100. Advisory only; it sizes nothing.

SCHEMA
The document must validate against this JSON Schema:
{{ schema }}

RETURN
{"steps": [ ... ]}
and nothing else.

task.description: The caller's task, verbatim (spec §9: caller prompts are passed through unmodified).

classification.description: The trajectory's declared data classification: public, internal or confidential.

tools.description: The trajectory allowlist rendered by Python as one line per tool with its registered description, so the model declares names it did not invent.

tiers.description: The configured tiers rendered by Python as one line per tier: name, local or remote, and the classification ceiling.

max_steps.description: planning.max_plan_steps, the upper bound on step count.

schema.description: PromptCadence's committed plan schema (domain/plan.schema.json), shown to the model. Shown, never handed to LoadCoach for validation (ADR-0041).

expectations: A single JSON object with a `steps` array, validated by PromptCadence against PLAN_SCHEMA and lifecycle §4.1's five rules.

metadata.change_reason: First version. The rules restated here are statements of the validator, not the validator: domain/plan.py decides, and this text exists so an honest model can satisfy checks it would otherwise fail by accident.
